newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon holds Palestinians over Katyusha attack.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon holds Palestinians over Katyusha attack.

text.p: Lebanese authorities are interrogating two radical Palestinian guerrillas detained on suspicion of firing a Katyusha rocket into Israel this week, judicial sources said on Friday.

Lebanese leaders, anxious to avoid escalation of violence between Moslem guerrillas and Israel in south Lebanon, earlier called for investigations into Wednesday's cross-border attack which the Jewish state has blamed the Lebanese government for.

The sources confirmed a report carried by Beirut's official National News Agency that two members of the Damascus-based Democratic Front for the Liberation of Palestine (DFLP) were arrested on Thursday in south Lebanon and were being questioned over the incident.
In Damascus, a spokesman for the group -- which opposes the Arab-Israeli peace process -- on Friday denied responsibility for the attack.

"The Democratic Front for the Liberation of Palestine did not fire any Katyushas against northern Israel," the DFLP spokesman told Reuters. He said the DFLP had not received any information about the arrest of two of its members in Lebanon.

It was the second Katyusha attack against Israel since an April 1996 ceasefire understanding that ended a 17-day Israeli blitz on Lebanon. The U.S.-brokered understanding banned attacks against civilians in northern Israel and south Lebanon.

Israeli officials have said that Beirut was to blame for the rocket attack. An aide to Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said on Thursday the Israeli army would do whatever was necessary to restore calm.

Lebanon's Parliament Speaker Nabih Berri, who also heads the pro-Syrian Amal Movement, was quoted earlier on Friday as saying that neither his Shi'ite group nor the pro-Iranian Hizbollah had fired the Soviet-made rockets into the western Galilee.

"It (Katyusha) was fired by factions that must be pinpointed through a thorough investigation and must be held accountable for what they are doing," Berri told members of the Lebanese Press Association on Thursday.
"This matter can cause unrest that we do not need, especially after the commitments in the April understanding over this and other issues," Berri added.

Hizbollah and Amal, both of which are fighting the Israeli occupation of a border zone in south Lebanon, have denied any links to Wednesday's incident. The DFLP and other Damascus-based groups have bases in south Lebanon which they use to launch attacks on the Jewish state.

Lebanese President Elias Hrawi was quoted by the daily an-Nahar as saying: "Israel must not be given a pretext to undertake new assaults. Firing Katyushas is useless militarily and it does not hurt Israel but can harm Lebanon."
Israel has filed a complaint over the incident with a five-nation group monitoring the April ceasefire.

A similar mysterious rocket attack took place on December 13 which Hizbollah and Lebanon-based radical Palestinian groups have denied links to. The ceasefire monitors verified the incident but did not hold Lebanon directly responsible.
